problem: Production Source Snapshot accepted a Git-linked Netlify build, but Netlify later marked the deploy Skipped. The workflow then exited before reaching its already-authorized direct MCP deploy fallback, leaving current main merged but not production-proven.
root_cause: The canonical production workflow treated acceptance of the preferred linked-build transport as exclusive ownership of the deployment attempt. Both linked-deploy error and bounded-readback timeout terminated with exit 78, so the direct MCP fallback below those branches was unreachable precisely when it was needed.
failed_approaches: Rotating the Netlify MCP proxy fixed the 401 authentication failure but did not address a later provider-side Skipped linked deploy.
Waiting longer could not make the skipped deploy publish because Netlify had already terminalized it as Skipped.
prevention: Transport acceptance is not production success; only exact production identity/readback is terminal proof.
When the preferred linked-build transport errors, is skipped, or fails bounded exact-SHA readback, continue automatically to the existing authorized direct MCP fallback.
Keep exact release.json SHA/context/deploy-id and production browser verification after any failover.
Keep authentication failures distinct from provider skip/build failures.
terminal_rule: Do not mark LIVE_BEWEZEN until the recovery is protected-merged, current main is deployed, and exact production/provider/browser readback is green.
